question: In an infant with unilateral aphakia after congenital cataract surgery, bilateral aphakic spectacles are the preferred first-line optical correction to prevent amblyopia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: FALSE. Bilateral aphakic spectacles would cause intolerable aniseikonia in unilateral aphakia. For unilateral infantile aphakia, a contact lens on the aphakic eye + occlusion therapy of the fellow eye is the standard approach. Secondary IOL is deferred to avoid refractive unpredictability during eye growth.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — FALSE. In unilateral infantile aphakia, aphakic spectacles cause severe aniseikonia (large image-size difference between the two eyes) that is visually intolerable. The preferred approach is a CONTACT LENS on the aphakic eye from as early as possible, combined with occlusion therapy of the fellow eye to prevent amblyopia. Secondary IOL implantation is typically deferred until age 2 or later.
